prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Britain is a great country headed in the wrong direction under Labour’s wrong values: too much waste, tax and talk; too little discipline, accountability and control. Conservatives will act, rewarding people who do the right thing, extending choice, devolving power and securing a decent society.

- Value for money and lower taxes: Wage war on waste, saving £12bn by 2007–08; use £8bn to cut borrowing and £4bn for immediate tax cuts. Spend at least as much as Labour on the NHS, schools, transport and development, and more on police, defence and pensions—while increasing total spending more slowly. Halve council tax bills for millions of pensioners; restore the basic state pension link to earnings; keep Winter Fuel Payments and free TV licences. Promote saving via Lifetime Savings Accounts; strengthen company pensions (opt-out defaults; unclaimed assets to support victims of scheme failures). Deregulate with regulatory budgets and sunset reviews; end gold-plating of EU rules; restore opt-out from the Social Chapter. Keep Bank of England independence; keep the pound; no to the euro.

- Families, childcare and schools: Trust parents with flexible childcare support (up to £50/week per under-5 through the tax credit; more workplace nurseries; clubs for older children) and flexible maternity pay. Restore discipline: heads control admissions and expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; cut teacher paperwork. Money follows the pupil; slimmer, rigorous curriculum; publish marks with grades; broaden qualifications, boost vocational status (300,000 grants). More PE and healthier food (ban junk food). Expand good schools (600,000 new places), protect special schools, scrap university fees and the admissions regulator.

- NHS: More investment (+£34bn in first Parliament), less bureaucracy (fewer PCTs, scrap SHAs and targets). Put professionals and patients in charge: funding follows the patient; free hospitals to specialise; bring back matrons with power to clean up wards; protect community hospitals; end waiting lists as we know them. Support carers; fair partnership for long-term care; improve dentistry; health checks for long-stay non-EU migrants—an NHS for the nation.

- Law and order: 5,000 extra police a year; elected police commissioners; slash paperwork; zero tolerance. End early release; 20,000 new prison places; honesty in sentencing. Expand drug rehab (25,000 residential places); reverse cannabis reclassification. Robust counter-terror leadership via a Homeland Security Minister.

- Controlled immigration: Take back control of borders with 24/7 port surveillance and a British Border Control Police. Australian-style points system prioritising needed skills. Modernise asylum: process outside the UK, take a fair UNHCR share, set an annual overall limit approved by Parliament; repatriate powers from Brussels, withdraw from the 1951 Convention.

- Accountability and communities: Abolish regional assemblies; strengthen Parliament; cut MPs by 20%; English votes for English laws. Devolve planning and enforce against illegal traveller camps. Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership. End Labour’s war on motorists; modernise roads; sensible speed-camera use; longer rail franchises. Protect Green Belt; build on brownfield; phase out HFCs; cut VED for low-emission cars; boost renewables and efficiency.

- Rural and farming: Free vote to overturn the hunting ban. Honest food labelling; insist Little Red Tractor in public procurement; reform CAP; strengthen animal welfare.

- Britain in the world: Spend £2.7bn more than Labour on the front line; preserve regiments and key warships; NATO first. Be honest about war; stay to help rebuild Iraq; pursue Middle East peace. No to the EU Constitution and the euro; restore national control over employment law and fisheries; widen EU through enlargement. Lead on open markets, law and democracy; meet 0.7% aid target by 2013 with more national control.

Day One: start hiring more police; bring back matrons; cut waste and taxes; empower heads to expel; begin 24-hour port security; set a referendum date to reject the EU Constitution.

It’s time for action—so the hardworking, law-abiding majority are rewarded, not punished.
